item.title: Not quite the same Bayern benchmark
item.description: Not quite the same Bayern benchmark Unfortunate in losing two talismans to injury, sling-wearing Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany had no experienced striker to call upon as his side tried to break down a dogged and determined 1. FC Köln in what would eventually end as a 1-1 stalemate on Friday night. Injuries to both Harry Kane and Michael Olise – in addition to Luis Díaz’s absence – exposed a glaring lack of depth at the business end of the pitch. Nathaniel Brown’s first-half equaliser came from nothing, while Lennart Karl and Tim Binder offered little of note throughout the second period. With the Ballon d'Or winner and a certain flying Frenchman nowhere in sight, proceedings at the Allianz Arena suddenly seemed a far cry from previous seasons. Dayot Upamecano’s reaction upon being replaced by Minjae Kim summed up the entire evening: one of clear, unadulterated frustration stemming in large part from a lack of rhythm or penetration. Credit has to go to the visitors for remaining steadfast in their efforts to earn something from this encounter. However, the second 45 minutes was crying out for a physical presence similar to that of Nicolas Jackson or the tenacity in close quarters of Raphaël Guerreiro. Despite enjoying more than two-thirds of the ball, Bayern registered a disappointing return of just two shots on target. Jamal Musiala, introduced with 20 minutes left to play, was largely ineffectual. With odds even in the closing stages, the expected flurry of corners and unrelenting pressure bearing down on the Südkurve failed to materialise. Leon Goretzka’s industrious nature, so often displayed even during the briefest of cameos, may have helped on that front. Naturally, an array of injuries to key personnel can decimate and eventually derail the best of sides. Calling on 19-year-old striker Noah Codjo-Evora with a matter of moments to go prompted a few raised eyebrows, while the sight of a previously exiled Sacha Boey on the bench serves as a constant reminder of pre-season transfer struggles. Fortunately, it was confirmed that Olise only suffered a bruised foot. On the other hand, Kane is set for his first significant spell on the sidelines since arriving in Munich after tearing an ankle ligament – the same injury recently suffered by Ismael Saibari. With the long-awaited return of Díaz next week, there will be an outlet on each flank but still a rather complex puzzle to solve down the middle.

item.title: Drivers limited to 27 laps for tyres in Qatar
item.description: Drivers were limited to 25 laps for each set of tyres in last year's Qatar Grand Prix [Getty Images] Formula 1 drivers will be limited to a maximum of 27 laps on a set of tyres at next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix. The decision is caused by concern over the integrity of the Pirelli tyres on the high-speed Lusail track, which has a series of demanding, long-duration corners. It means teams will have to make at least two pit stops during the 57-lap grand prix, as was the case last year. The limit applies on a single set of tyres whenever it is used across sessions. So mileage done in practice or qualifying, for example, would limit the number of laps that could be done on a set of tyres in the race. Pirelli said the limit was longer then last year's 25 laps because of the reduced downforce levels of the 2026 cars compared with 2025. "The increase has been made possible by the lower load levels recorded so far on the current generation of cars and by a further reinforcement of the tyre construction," a statement said. Last year, the limit led to a major strategic error by McLaren, who lost a win because they failed to pit under a safety car period when everyone else did. It is the third time in four years Pirelli has imposed a tyre-duration limit at Qatar, where running wide over flat kerbs in addition to the high-speed nature of the track is especially demanding for the tyres. Pirelli described the decision as a "precautionary measure" that was "linked to the unique characteristics of the Lusail circuit, which is particularly demanding in terms of energy loads, thermal stress and tread wear". In terms of the way the limit will be imposed, the statement said: "Laps will be counted cumulatively across all track sessions, including any laps completed under the safety car or virtual safety car. "As far as the grand prix is concerned, all laps completed from the start signal to the chequered flag will count towards the total. "Reconnaissance laps, formation laps and any laps completed after the end of the race will not be included. "In all other track sessions, any lap that has been started but not completed will nevertheless be counted as a full lap. "Should a team assemble a tyre set using tyres that have covered different mileages, the tyre with the highest lap count will determine the mileage attributed to that set." item.title: Antonelli fastest but penalty leaves Verstappen on pole
item.description: Kimi Antonelli won both the previous two grands prix in the United States this season, in Miami and Austin [Getty Images] Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli was fastest in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix but a grid penalty will hand pole position to Red Bull's Max Verstappen. Antonelli, running at the back of the pack of cars in qualifying and maximising his tow, beat Verstappen by 0.258 seconds. But the new world champion has a five-place grid penalty for using more than permitted number of engine components and will start sixth. The Italian's team-mate George Russell was just 0.073secs behind Verstappen and will start alongside the Dutchman on the front row. McLaren's Lando Norris qualified fourth, and will start third, ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar. Both Ferraris were eliminated in the second session and qualified 11th and 12th with Charles Leclerc ahead of Lewis Hamilton. Each will be promoted a place by a 10-place penalty for McLaren's Oscar Piastri, who qualified seventh. Racing Bulls' rookie Arvid Lindblad, sixth fastest, is the last driver to be promoted as a result of Antonelli's penalty. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson will start seventh with Alpine's Pierre Gasly eighth and Franco Colapinto ninth. 'Somebody has to stand up to that guy' - and Russell has his chance in Vegas Drivers limited to 27 laps for tyres in Qatar Antonelli's final run did not start auspiciously as he and Russell became tangled up with the Alpines and Racing Bulls as they sought the best track position to optimise the slipstream effect. Antonelli ended up the last driver to run and made it to the line with only one second to spare before the chequered flag, one second behind Lindblad. Normally, being so close to the car in front would be a compromise but in Las Vegas it magnified the tow effect and Antonelli leapt to the front. "That was all the tow," he said over the radio after being told he was on pole. "Starting the lap, I was only one second behind the car in front and I thought I was screwed," he said. "But the tow is so powerful here." Verstappen, who has won two of the three Las Vegas Grands Prix, said: "I have been struggling with some weird issues that were also in the car in Brazil and just trying to get my head around how to deal with that. "In qualifying we managed to make it work. Had a solid qualifying. My first lap in qualifying was pretty much as good as it could be with the tow, so to be on the front row is good for us. "It was solid in the corners, and you have a bit of dirty air, but it is insane how much you gain on the straights." item.title: 'Somebody has to stand up to that guy' - and Russell has his chance in Vegas
item.description: Max Verstappen (left) and George Russell (right) will start on the front row in the Las Vegas Grand Prix [Getty Images] The Las Vegas Grand Prix will start with two drivers on the front row who dislike each other - and after qualifying one said of the other that "somebody has got to stand up to that guy". "That guy" is Max Verstappen, who starts his Red Bull from pole position. The driver criticising him is Mercedes' George Russell, who lines up second. Both were promoted after the fastest qualifier, new world champion Kimi Antonelli, was demoted by a five-place grid penalty for exceeding his engine allocation for the season. Russell's beef stemmed from an incident in final practice, in which Verstappen overtook the Mercedes on the Las Vegas Strip, then veered in front of him into Turn 14. Russell, unhappy with the Dutchman's behaviour, dived down the Red Bull's inside on braking for the corner, got alongside, and then made his displeasure known by pushing Verstappen wide, the two cars making light contact. They were called to the stewards to discuss the incident. Verstappen was given a warning having been found to have made an "unpredictable change of direction under braking". After qualifying, Russell told Sky Italia: "I think the warning was fine. There's nothing in the rules to say that you cannot overtake someone who is starting their lap but when you do this, you are screwing this person over. "He does this week in, week out, with many drivers. Everybody accepts it and I am not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they are bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody has got to stand up to that guy." Russell's comments were not put to Verstappen as he had finished his media commitments by the time they emerged into wider knowledge in Las Vegas. Asked about the incident in the official news conference, Verstappen said: "Nothing happened." When Verstappen spoke to the Dutch media, he was again reluctant to be drawn on it. But asked whether it gave him extra motivation to beat Russell in the race, he said: "I don't need any extra motivation." George Russell and Max Verstappen battling for track position during final practice in Las Vegas [Getty Images] These two have history. This incident is almost exactly two years since they fell out in public following a row at the Qatar Grand Prix where Verstappen felt Russell had stepped over the line to get him a penalty that demoted him from pole position. They exchanged insults. Russell, in remarks that echo those from Las Vegas, said: "People have been bullied by Max for years now." Verstappen called Russell a "backstabber" and a "loser". That was just the latest in a series of incidents - after a clash in Azerbaijan in 2022, Verstappen called Russell "Princess George" in a spat the Briton called "a little bit pathetic". item.description: Dripping Springs' Jacob Bremmer jumps to catch a touchdown pass above Judson's Myles Wisdom during the Class 6A Division II second round playoff game at Pieper's Warrior Coliseum on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. Dripping Springs defeated Judson 59-28. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) Dripping Springs tallied 603 yards of total offense in overwhelming Judson 59-28 Friday in the Class 6A Division II area playoff at Pieper's Warrior Stadium. Judson took the early lead in the first quarter before Dripping Springs took control behind running back Frank Accetta, who rushed for 209 yards and three touchdowns. The Tigers (10-1) take on Pharr-San Juan-Alamo North in the third round next week. Pharr-San Juan-Alamo North defeated Warren 46-15 in second-round action on Friday. Judson (6-5) ended its season with its deepest playoff run since 2023, when it also lost to Dripping Springs 38-34 in the second round. "It didn't go the way that we wanted because we didn't do the things necessary to make those kind of plays," Judson coach Vernon Hughes said. "I don't think we did what we needed to do in all three phases. We just kept making mental mistake after mental mistake after mental mistake and whenever you're playing really good football teams, you can't beat good football teams playing that way." Judson's Kayden Graham runs the ball during the Class 6A Division II second round playoff game against Dripping Springs at Pieper's Warrior Coliseum on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. Dripping Springs defeated Judson 59-28. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) Even in defeat, Hughes said his squad kept playing and never gave up. "I'm proud of the way that the guys played," Hughes said. "We showed some resilience. The kids never gave up. I mean (Dripping Springs) is a really good football team. The Rockets were led Jay'maree Bowens, who caught seven passes for 120 yards and two scores, and senior running back Kayden Graham, who rushed for 106 yards on 19 carries, capping his final season in a Judson uniform with 1,722 yards and 23 touchdowns. Judson got off to a promising start, as a fumble recovery at the Dripping Springs 30 led to a Bo Amador 20-yard field goal, putting Judson up 3-0 with 5:08 in the first quarter. Dripping Springs tied the game on its ensuing possession on a 22-yard field goal from Jack Miller. Dripping Springs started to pull away in the third quarter, scoring 28 points in the frame. item.title: Giorgio Scalvini: Man United battling Liverpool, Chelsea for Atalanta defender
item.description: Giorgio Scalvini: Man United battling Liverpool, Chelsea for Atalanta defender Manchester United struggles at the back are likely to be addressed by INEOS in 2027, with fans already clamouring for defensive additions at the turn of the year. The Red Devils have let in 30 goals across competitions this season, including 19 in 10 games in the Premier League, where they have slipped to 18th in the table. The situation has prompted drastic actions from the club hierarchy – Michael Carrick has been removed from his position, while Mauricio Pochettino has been appointed as his replacement. While there is optimism that the Argentine can pull the club out of dire straits, it is also evident that he will need backing in the transfer market to successfully implement his tactics. United need defensive reinforcements All signs indicate that defensive reinforcements will be at the centre of United’s transfer activity in 2027 and for good reason too. Harry Maguire is on the wrong side of 30 and out of contract at the end of this season. Lisandro Martínez has blown hot and cold this year, and will also enter the final six months of his contract in January. The Argentine remains linked with an exit at the turn of the year. United were reportedly interested in Atalanta’s Giorgio Scalvini in the summer, and it now appears that they are ready to return for the Italian in 2027. The report acknowledges that there were concerns earlier this year whether the 22-year-old could return to his best after suffering an ACL injury in 2024 and spending considerable time on the sidelines with various knocks. item.title: ‘It’s a lie!’ – Mykhailo Mudryk hits back at Andriy Shevchenko as civil war erupts over banned substance suspension
item.description: Mykhailo Mudryk Chelsea 2026 - Getty Mykhailo Mudryk has sensationally accused Andriy Shevchenko of lying as the bitter dispute over the winger's doping ban escalates. The Tottenham Hotspur loanee claims he has firm evidence proving the Ukrainian Association of Football deliberately misled the investigation into his positive test. Mudryk brands Shevchenko a liar The bitter fallout surrounding Mudryk's lengthy suspension for a doping violation has taken an explosive turn. The Tottenham winger has publicly accused Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) president Shevchenko of lying. Mudryk, who is currently on a one-season loan from Chelsea, has been handed a suspension that runs from November 2024 to July 2026. The suspension was issued after he tested positive for the banned substance meldonium. The forward firmly blames the UAF for his failed test and subsequent exile. He believes the prohibited substance entered his system while he was away on international duty with Ukraine. Shevchenko alleges false blame plot The war of words escalated dramatically following recent comments from Shevchenko . The former Chelsea and AC Milan striker alleged that Mudryk's representatives repeatedly asked a UAF employee to falsely take the blame for the positive test. Shevchenko branded the winger's complaints as a "baseless slander against our people" and demanded a retraction. However, Mudryk fiercely hit back in a statement released on Friday to deny the claims. "Neither I nor my representatives made any such request," Mudryk declared, as quoted by BBC , categorically rejecting the accusation. Winger claims proof of cover-up Mudryk insists that the UAF actively attempted to mislead the investigation to distance the governing body from the scandal. He also accused the federation of being repeatedly slow to respond and deliberately withholding crucial documents from his lawyers. "My team and I repeatedly asked the UAF to help establish how I might have been exposed to meldonium and who, if anyone, might have been responsible," Mudryk explained. "In several letters to the UAF at the time, my lawyers made clear that we were seeking truthful information that could be independently verified. One of those letters was leaked to the media by the UAF earlier today and clearly shows that my lawyers wanted 'true, verifiable and reliable information. "Further, the UAF were repeatedly unhelpful and even attempted to mislead my team in order to distance themselves from the case. For example, UAF staff testified at my hearing that I was not using the UAF's supplements and Mr Shevchenko has repeated that assertion in his statement - but I have WhatsApp messages that prove that I was using their products during their training camps. That is, I have evidence to prove that their repeated assertions are wrong." item.title: Lens’ Robin Risser attracting Juventus and Inter interest, PL clubs also in hunt
item.description: Lens’ Robin Risser attracting Juventus and Inter interest, PL clubs also in hunt Lens keeper Robin Risser has had a significant rise to stardom in the last 12 months and has also managed to feature in the Champions League this season. As his stocks keep going up, interest in the Frenchman is only growing, with Inter, Juventus and several Premier League clubs in the hunt. Tuttomercatoweb provide details about the 21-year-old’s situation, reporting that the Nerazzurri have been following Risser for many months now. They’re unhappy with Josep Martinez’s form and could seek a replacement, which can turn out to be the Lens star himself. Milan have previously made contact for the keeper too but now, it is Juventus who are monitoring Risser closely. While they do have Guglielmo Vicario as the first-choice, the Lens man can become an option in the future. Most importantly, Risser is currently at the top of the Manchester City’s shortlist, with Gigio Donnarumma struggling. There is a chance even Liverpool could chose to invest in Risser, as competition from Bayern Munich also grows, with the Bavarians seeking to solve their keeper worries for the next ten years. For now, Lens’ price tag stands at €40 million, which could be complicated for Serie A clubs right now. But is clear the player has witnessed growth and a big move could soon be on the horizon. Kaustubh Pandey – GIFN

item.title: Real Madrid defender Eder Militao reveals what makes Jude Bellingham special: ‘Super competitive’
item.description: Real Madrid defender Eder Militao reveals what makes Jude Bellingham special: ‘Super competitive’ With all the internationals back in training, Real Madrid are set to take on Celta Vigo later today at the Santiago Bernabeu. Jose Mourinho has some big decisions to make ahead of kickoff, not only involving Vinicius Jr. and Yan Diomande but also involving internationals who played a hectic role in the recent hiatus. One such player is Jude Bellingham, who played a total of 173 minutes in two games during the recent international break. Militao praises Bellingham Real Madrid defender Eder Militao spoke to the media in a recent interview where he opened up on how Jude Bellingham is as a teammate behind the scenes. Quite unsurprisingly, he described the Englishman as a player who trains with the same intensity that he shows on the field. Militao is slowly returning. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) “Jude Bellingham? He’s super competitive, even in training,” he said, h/t Madrid Xtra . Elaborating on the monstrous mentality Bellingham has and how the dressing room mocks him for the same, Militao jovially said, “He hates losing. We always joke that he’s like an old man.” Elaborating on his recent interaction with the midfield star, Militao said, “I told Jude Bellingham, ‘Man, I’m so proud to have you on my team, seriously. You’re playing at an absolutely ridiculous level. It’s like you see the game in slow motion. “ Everything you do, even when someone tries to nick the ball off you, it’s like you’ve already spotted them six days beforehand.'” “He thanked me for my words. Jude likes Brazil. He’s always hanging out with us,” he added. Coming off a special hiatus Bellingham was electric against Spain. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Jude Bellingham was on duty with the English national team over the past few weeks and played a big part in his side’s two massive wins in the same period. Against Croatia, Bellingham assisted Morgan Rogers for the team’s opening goal in their 2-1 win. The bigger game notably came against Spain, and Bellingham was key in the result that saw Spain’s first defeat in over two years. On the night, he assisted one goal and ensured England’s attack stayed incisive enough to bypass the Spanish dominance.

item.title: Nick Bosa Given Candid Assessment of 49ers Future Amid Struggles
item.description: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) Getty Nick Bosa hasn’t been the dominant force the San Francisco 49ers need on their defensive line, particularly when it comes to pressuring opposing quarterbacks. Given his massive contract, questions are beginning to emerge about whether Bosa’s long-term future in San Francisco could be in doubt if his production doesn’t improve. This season so far, Bosa has played 172 total snaps on defense for the 49ers, leading to a 71.8 overall PFF defensive grade . Moreover, the veteran edge rusher has recorded 11 total pressures, zero sacks, 10 hurries, six stops, six solo tackles, and one QB hit. As a result, Mark Willard and Dan Dibley of 95.7 The Game shared their outlook on what the future holds for Bosa with the 49ers. “He’s not at a minimum right now, and very possibly, probably never again will he be who he used to be,” Willard said in a Nov. 19 video from 95.7 The Game. “Now, does that mean that he’s not potentially still rreally productive? “Put it this way: I don’t think the Niners are as far along as a lot of fans are with the idea that they’re trading or getting rid of Nick Bosa after this season. He is still their best pass rusher, and I don’t think it’s terribly close.” 49ers Better Off Reworking Nick Bosa’s Contract Meanwhile, Dibley believes that the Niners are better off reworking his deal rather than having to deal with the ramifications of having to cut ties with him. Moreover, Dibley notes that Bosa isn’t a bad player; he’s probably not worth what the 49ers are currently paying him. “When the cap hit is so unwieldy that you’re more likely to rework the deal to stretch him out and try to make it so that eventually, when you do want to move on from him, the cap hit will be less than about $45 million, which is what it would be if you went ahead and did that,” Dibley said. “He is still a serviceable pass rusher. If you think about what ACL recovery is like, the first year is not always roses and sunshine. Sometimes it takes time to get back.” Nick Bosa Is Having a Reality Check Moment Dibley notes that Bosa is currently dealing with what all players deal with as they approach their 30s, which is that what worked for them in their early to mid 20s to mid 20s isn’t working anymore. As a result, it’s on the 49ers’ edge rusher to adapt or get left behind. “Also, the idea of him coasting, I do think, is a bit of a reality check,” Dibley added. “You were elite, you’ve been elite all the way back to high school, and now you come back from your third ACL and think, well, I can still do A, B, and C. “You start to do it, and only four games in, you’re realizing that you’re not able to get around the corner like you used to [and] you can’t bend like you used to. item.title: Wolff dismisses lack of tow for Russell as Verstappen inherits pole
item.description: Toto Wolff believes George Russell was in the right position to claim pole when asked why Mercedes decided not to give the Briton a tow from Kimi Antonelli in Q3. Over the course of the session, Russell asked whether he could receive a tow from his teammate Antonelli, considering that the Italian has a five-place grid penalty for tomorrow's race. However, Mercedes did not arrange that for him. Antonelli was the last to start his lap and, after receiving a good tow from Racing Bulls, set the fastest time in Q3. As a result, Max Verstappen will inherit pole position , while Russell will line up alongside him on the front row at the Las Vegas Grand Prix . Speaking to Sky Sports, Mercedes team principal Wolff said: "Actually, George, for me, had the perfect position. He was four seconds behind the car in front. We need to find out because I think there was some kind of… Turns 7-8-9, whether that was a mistake or something else happened, we need to… I don’t know, to be honest, but it looked like the ideal position for a pole lap, because he was quickest all the time." Antonelli surprised Wolff today - Photo: Race Pictures Antonelli surprised Wolff today - Photo: Race Pictures Wolff stunned by Antonelli's pole lap With the two Mercedes, two Racing Bulls and two Alpine cars so close together on track during the final warm-up lap, Antonelli decided to let the others pass. The world champion just managed to start his flying lap before the clock ticked down to zero. “We have absolutely no clue [how he set the fastest lap]. We thought Kimi was either going to miss the lap or he’s going to be way too close to Lindblad. He crossed the line 1.4 seconds behind, and that was basically it. item.description: Motorsport photo Lando Norris lamented McLaren ’s “shocking” straightline speed after missing out on pole at the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix. The 2025 world champion was fourth fastest on Friday night in Nevada and 0.351s off pacesetter Kimi Antonelli, with Max Verstappen and George Russell also quicker. Norris’s deficit largely came in the final sector where he was 0.776s slower than his world champion successor, despite being faster in the first two - even quickest of all in the second. But the final sector is usually what defines a lap around the low-downforce Vegas street track due to its 1.2-mile flat-out Strip section, plus the 0.5-mile straight ahead of the final corner. “We're just shocking in the straights,” said Norris, who will start from third due to Antonelli’s five-place grid drop for a new internal combustion engine. “Like, horrendous in the straights. My lap was very good. It was easily my best lap. But we're just, yeah, to Kimi we're eight-tenths off in the last sector. Oscar Piastri, McLaren, Lando Norris, McLaren Oscar Piastri, McLaren, Lando Norris, McLaren “He has a perfect tow and he does a very good job. But comparing to most other people, we're too far off. “I have to start my lap 1.5 seconds off the car ahead, which means in every corner I'm losing at least half a tenth to a tenth because of how much downforce I'm losing. “There's obviously a bigger gain at the end of the day in having a good slipstream, but we're having to make up for a really terrible loss of straightline speed - and therefore we have to harm our cornering speed. “So we just haven't got the right balance, all in all, in terms of downforce, drag. item.title: ‘He Let Everybody Know He Has Beef With Joe Buck’ — Former Eagles All-Pro Understands Why Troy Aikman Went Scorched Earth
item.description: Aug 5, 2023; Canton, OH, USA; Troy Aikman arrives on the red carpet for the 2023 Pro Football Hall of Fame Enshrinement at Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium. © Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports We’re past the halfway mark of the season, and while there’s been a lot of action on the field, some animosity in the broadcasting game has also been drawing attention. We’re, of course, talking about Troy Aikman’s beef with his Monday Night Football colleague, Joe Buck. Amid reports that the two had a verbal altercation ahead of Week 5’s primetime Los Angeles Rams-Buffalo Bills game, Aikman decided to kinda-sorta pour jet fuel on the fire this week during an appearance on 96.7 The Ticket, when he said, “Joe’s always wanted a one-man booth.” While that was a light-hearted throwaway line, the damage was already done, as their beef spilled out of the broadcast booth and onto the radio. Hugh Douglas came away impressed by the way Aikman did it. Hugh Douglas, the former Philadelphia Eagles All-Pro defensive end, made it clear he was impressed by how Aikman went about it all. Why Hugh Douglas Called Troy Aikman’s Move ‘Gangster’ At first, Douglas said he heard the clip as Aikman airing a grievance while his broadcast partner tried to smooth it over. “I heard the snippet and I was like, wow, he took that beef to the radio and Joe Buck was trying to, you know, calm it down,” Douglas said on 94WIP . His view changed when he was told that Buck had not been on the air with Aikman at all. “But when you told me he wasn’t even there, I’m like, that was kind of gangster of Troy.” What stood out to Douglas was that Aikman made no attempt to keep the dispute private. “He let everybody know that he has beef with Joe Buck,” Douglas said, adding that Aikman’s message amounted to “Hey, yeah, we got beef.” IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Douglas also questioned whether Buck would take the fight, so to speak, to Aikman, wondering aloud, “Is Joe Buck about that life? That’s what we’re talking about.” Can Buck and Aikman Last the Season? Then the talk turned to what comes next. Douglas was asked whether the pair can stay together through the rest of the regular season, at least one playoff game, and the Super Bowl. Super Bowl LXI is mere months away, and the timing of Aikman’s comments could not have been worse. Just days earlier, ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro said that he was “disappointed” by how the media was reporting on the tension between the two veteran broadcasters. Pitaro recruited the pair from Fox, where Buck and Aikman called six Super Bowls over a two-decade stint at the network. Per The Athletic, ESPN and Buck agreed to a new six-year, $108 million deal, a roughly 20% increase over his previous contract. Aikman, meanwhile, does not have a new deal in place, a development that has been reported to be at the center of the tension between the two. item.title: 'Making my job easier': CSK head coach Zaheer Khan breaks silence on MS Dhoni's 'unexpected' retirement
item.description: Chennai Super Kings head coach Zaheer Khan has admitted that MS Dhoni's decision to retire from playing in the Indian Premier League came as a surprise to him, while describing the end of the former captain's playing career as an emotional moment for the franchise. Dhoni will no longer take the field for CSK but will remain associated with the five-time champions as their team mentor from IPL 2027. Zaheer said the team would miss having Dhoni as a player but was looking forward to working with him in his new role. "It's been an emotional week for all of us, with mixed feelings. Every year, you're hoping that MS is going to be seen playing a role for the team this season. He will be, but in a different avatar, and hence the mixed feelings. "I think the journey he has had in cricket has been amazing. Srinivasan rightly said that there is no CSK without MS, and that surely is the case," Zaheer said in a video uploaded on CSK's YouTube channel. Dhoni's retirement from playing was confirmed on November 17, when CSK announced that he would take up the role of team mentor. Zaheer said he was also looking forward to having Dhoni's experience and guidance as he takes charge of the team ahead of the next season. "It's mixed feelings for me personally because you're not going to see him as part of the playing team. But I'm excited that he's going to be sharing the burden with me, making my job easier, guiding us in the right direction and being a mentor to us. "So, yeah, excited about that, looking ahead, but also emotional about the decision he has taken," Zaheer added. Dhoni led CSK to five IPL titles and two Champions League T20 crowns. However, he did not play a single match during the 2026 season because of fitness concerns. While CSK owner Rupa Gurunath had earlier revealed that Dhoni had indicated he might not return as a player, Zaheer said he had not seriously considered the possibility. His focus, he explained, had been on preparing the squad and planning for the upcoming season. "Not at all. I think, for a couple of reasons, it was the last year of this cycle. So maybe, looking ahead at a fresh cycle, those kind of thoughts would have popped into my head," Zaheer said. "But right now, I wasn't even thinking about it. Obviously, you're looking at the season, you're looking at the stack-up of your team, the playing XI. I haven't personally given it a thought because, you know, it's MS. He knows what is the right thing to do and when is the time to act upon a certain thing. "So I was not really spending my time and energy going in that direction. Whatever it is, it's going to be his decision. I'm planning for the season. "So, yes, it was unexpected for me personally when he did mention it in a very, very subtle way, as you know, he doesn't like to create massive news out of it. item.title: Chiefs Could Add Another Veteran WR After Bad News on Tyreek Hill
item.description: San Francisco 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk has been reinstated by the NFL Getty The Kansas City Chiefs have been seen as a likely landing spot for Tyreek Hill, but the veteran wide receiver’s slow recovery could push them to another late-season target. Hill has been working his way back from a devastating knee injury last season, and agent Drew Rosenhaus said this week that Hill is still not cleared to play. But the super-agent has another client who could soon hit the open market, one seen as a dark-horse candidate to join the Chiefs. Chiefs May Need to Change WR Plans In an appearance on The Russini Report this week, Rosenhaus told host Dianna Russini that San Francisco 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk is medically cleared and ready to play again. The only hitch is the 49ers, who made it clear that Aiyuk isn’t welcome back after his relationship with the team fell apart. Rosenhaus hinted that the 49ers will eventually waive Aiyuk, likely sending him to free agency. “I’m not sure what’s going to happen with waivers because of his current contract, but our instinct is that he’ll become a free agent and we’ll have options,” Rosenhaus said. “I’m not permitted to talk to teams, but based on my 38 years of experience and reading the tea leaves, I expect that he’ll have many suitors…but he would like to get out there and play as soon as possible.” The Chiefs have been floated as one of the teams that could be interested. Daniel Mader of The Sporting News suggested that Aiyuk could be an asset to Kansas City’s wide receiver room. “Expecting Aiyuk to immediately be the version of himself that finished with over 1,200 yards in 2023 is unrealistic, especially considering he hasn’t even been in an NFL facility in months,” Mader wrote. “But if Aiyuk can ramp back up a bit for a few weeks, by the tail end of the season, he could be a field-stretching weapon for Mahomes, averaging 14.6 yards per catch in his career.” Tyreek Hill Still Not Ready to Return The Chiefs did make one big addition to their wide receiver room, trading for Josh Downs before this season’s deadline. But many insiders expected them to take a run at Hill, who had a strong connection with Mahomes during his time in Kansas City. Rosenhaus told Russini that he couldn’t say when Hill would be ready to take the field again. “I really don’t have a timetable for him, because I respect the process. It’s not about putting any pressure on him directly or indirectly in terms of when he returns to play,” Rosenhaus said. item.title: Mexico drawn in Group B for 2027 U17 World Cup qualifiers which they will co-host
item.description: Da’vian Kimbrough | via @miseleccionsubs Mexico was named as one of the co-hosts of the 2027 U17 World Cup Qualifiers in which they were drawn in Group B. Mexico will face off against Costa Rica, Barbados and the Dominican Republic in a Group were the top two teams will qualify to the U17 World Cup. Mexico will be hosting Group A and Group B while Group C and D will be hosted by Honduras. CONCACAF has changed the format for the U17 World Cup qualifiers. After having 8 groups in which the winners of the group qualify to the World Cup, now it will be 4 groups of 4 teams in which the top two teams of each group will qualify to the World Cup. Two of the groups will be played in Mexico while the other two groups will play in Honduras. Mexico will host Group A and B, which will be played in the FMF headquarters in Toluca, the same venue that hosted Mexico’s group in the 2025 U17 World Cup qualifiers. Mexico was drawn in Group B along with Costa Rica, Barbados and the Dominican Republic. Mexico will start their tournament by facing Barbados on February 9th. Mexico will then face off against Costa Rica on February 11th and close out against the Dominican Republic on February 14th. All the tournaments matches will be played in Toluca in the FMF Headquarters stadium. Mexico will be heavy favorites to win the group and to qualify, not only as hosts but that the majority of the team should be the U15 team that won the last U15 CONCACAF Championship. Coach Yasser Corona, who was the one that coached that team to the title, will be the coach for the U17 team. Mexico will be playing a four nation tournament in December in preparation for the Qualifiers but the details of the tournament have yet to be released.

item.title: Nations Championship schedule, results and finals weekend permutations
item.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship has reached its last weekend of pool play with the finals weekend fate of the world’s top teams becoming clear. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action. South Africa and New Zealand are assured of a top-two finish in their group – but both were beaten in a stunning penultimate round of pool action. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how the tables stand ahead of finals weekend. What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. item.title: Juju Watkins & No. 4 USC take down undefeated Baylor at Intuit Dome
item.description: JuJu Watkins (USC) goes up for a layup against Baylor at Intuit Dome On a night of history for the Intuit Dome, Juju Watkins continued her own historic march in the scoring department. No. 4 USC (4-1) took down Baylor, 78-69, in the first ever women’s basketball game at Intuit Dome. “The opportunity to play in this building is amazing,” said Trojan junior guard, Ryann Bennett. “It didn’t feel real. I was looking at the scoreboard and was amazed every time.” Baylor arrived in Inglewood undefeated, and would leave with their first loss of the season at the hands of the Trojans. For Watkins, it was yet another game of scoring 30 points or more. She is now two more 30-point games away from tying the great Cheryl Miller for most in USC history. “Being able to follow in her (Miller) footsteps and bring another championship here is my goal,” Watkins said. She led all players with a double-double, scoring 36 points, along with 11 rebounds. The projected number one pick in next year’s WNBA draft also had six steals. “USC is a top five team for a reason, probably mainly because of Juju,” said Baylor Head Coach Nicki Collen. “Juju got us.” Early on, the Trojans found themselves in trouble. Baylor opened the game on a 8-0 run. The Bears would have their lead swell to 15 late in the 1st quarter. USC trailed 26-15 after the first ten minutes. In the 2nd quarter, USC clamped down defensively, bringing out the full-court press. At halftime, they would have the lead, outscoring Baylor 26-14 in the period. “(It’s good) to know that you have a team that can lock in and get stops,” said USC Head Coach Lindsay Gottlieb. “I thought our defensive effort after that first quarter was really, really good. And that allows our offense to get going.” Even though the Trojans would control the 2nd half, Baylor would only found themselves down by six with under five minute left to play. That’s when Watkins and company closed the door and left Intuit Dome with a win. “It's a once in a lifetime opportunity,” Watkins said after the historic matchup. “I was just really proud. And hopefully we get more women's games in here.” In some ways, christening the area for women’s basketball felt more important than the outcome of the game. “This is an unbelievable venue,” Cullen added. “When the lights popped off the (Intuit Dome) seats I was like, wow!” “To be a standalone one one game - not a double header, not adding a men's game or something, it shows the power of women's basketball, what USC women's basketball means in LA,” Gottlieb said.

item.description: Ryan Kavuma-McQueen joined Portsmouth on loan over the summer [Shutterstock] Explosive pace, infectious energy on the field and bundles of footballing ability. At just 17, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen has looked at home in the Championship since embarking on his first loan move away from Chelsea. With one senior appearance to his name at Stamford Bridge, the winger swapped west London for the south coast in August and has quickly become a fan favourite at Fratton Park. Indeed, Kavuma-McQueen was so impressive in a recent game against Sheffield United, Pompey boss John Mousinho admitted their tactic essentially became - pass him the ball as much as possible. "For a 17-year-old to come in and play as many games as he has done is a real achievement," the Portsmouth head coach told BBC Sport. "He's been brilliant to work with and has been absolutely unplayable in some games, for us it's now about getting him consistently to that level. "It's very easy to forget that he's only 17 because of the way that he plays and how he carries himself - overall it's been an excellent loan so far and we're really excited to see how he goes for the rest of the season." At international level, Kavuma-McQueen has played 31 matches for England's youth sides and scored 29 goals. One of his most recent for England Under-18s was a stunning strike that saw him beat a number of defenders with some smart footwork before launching a right-footed rocket into the top corner from 25 yards. For Portsmouth, he scored seven minutes into his first Championship start and has registered two assists, contributing to winning points for the Blues in games against Blackburn Rovers and Sheffield United. "No other so-called 'big six' Premier League club has a fully homegrown 17-year-old on loan in the Championship," said BBC football news reporter Nizaar Kinsella . "Securing a loan move was so important this summer, without European football, and with a large number of wide options available, opportunities were always likely to be limited at Chelsea." item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.title: How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊
item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
